title: Vector Physics MCQ — Page 55 (Q1–Q2)
notes:
**Q1. Which of the following is a scalar quantity?**

(a) Force
(b) Magnetic field
(c) Electric potential
(d) Magnetic moment

**Answer:** (c) Electric potential

**Explanation:** Electric potential is defined as work done per unit charge ($W/q$). Since both work and charge are scalar quantities, electric potential has only magnitude and no directional dependencies.

**Q2. Which of the following is a vector quantity?**

(a) Temperature
(b) Electric current
(c) Pressure
(d) Weight

**Answer:** (d) Weight

**Explanation:** Weight is a gravitational pull acting on a mass. It possesses both magnitude and a distinct, downward spatial vector direction targeting the center of gravity.
A scalar has magnitude only. Mass, temperature, energy, work, speed, electric charge and electric potential are scalars. They add by ordinary arithmetic.
A vector has magnitude and direction and must be added by the triangle or parallelogram rule. Displacement, velocity, acceleration, force, weight and momentum are vectors.
Electric potential is work per unit charge. Work and charge are both scalars, so potential is a scalar even though it is connected with the electric field, which is a vector.
Electric current has a direction in a wire, but currents do not follow the vector addition law when wires meet at an angle in the way forces do. In this course current is treated as a scalar.
confusion: A quantity with a direction word is not automatically a vector. It must obey vector addition.
Speed is scalar. Velocity is vector.

exercises.question: Classify mass, weight, speed and velocity. Give the reason for weight.
steps: Mass is an amount of matter and has no direction, so it is a scalar.
Weight is the force mg and points downward toward the Earth, so it is a vector.
Speed is the rate of covering distance and has no direction, so it is a scalar.
Velocity is displacement over time and has a direction, so it is a vector.
The deciding test is whether direction and the vector addition rule are required.
exercises.answer: Mass scalar, weight vector, speed scalar, velocity vector.

summary: Scalars have magnitude only. Vectors have magnitude and direction and add by the parallelogram rule. Potential, mass, speed, temperature and pressure are scalars. Weight, force, velocity and momentum are vectors. Current is treated as a scalar in this course.
